Unnamed: 1: System Cannot Power On (AC Indicator OFF)
Unnamed: 2: System does not respond. AC indicator on control panel is OFF.
Unnamed: 3: Is AC power cable properly connected and wall outlet supplying correct voltage?
Unnamed: 4: Outlet verified, AC connected — AC-DC assembly failure
Unnamed: 5: Check AC-DC output (5VSTB). Replace AC-DC Assembly (Power Box 115-047000-00)
Unnamed: 6: AC not connected or outlet faulty
Unnamed: 7: Verify wall outlet with test device; visual inspection of power cord (Appendix A Test 1). Correct power connection.
Unnamed: 8: 5VSTB output at AC-DC module; mains voltage at inlet
Unnamed: 10: Restore AC connection; OR replace AC-DC assembly (115-042951-00 or Power Box 115-047000-00)
Unnamed: 11: If replacing AC-DC does not resolve: suspected wiring fault — qualified electrician required

Unnamed: 1: System Cannot Power On (AC ON, Power Button No Response)
Unnamed: 2: AC indicator ON. Pressing power button — power-on/off indicator does NOT illuminate or blink. 3.3V/5V/12V indicators OFF.
Unnamed: 3: Does pressing power button cause any indicator to blink at all?
Unnamed: 4: No blink whatsoever — PC Carrier Board failure (90% probability per manual)
Unnamed: 5: Run Self-Test Z0201 (PC Module ↔ MF FPGA). Replace PC Carrier Board (115-033343-01). NOTE: requires OS upgrade to V5.0.
Unnamed: 6: Some indicator changes — refer to PWR-003 or PWR-004
Unnamed: 7: See PWR-003 (green blink) or PWR-004 (yellow blink) trees
Unnamed: 8: PWRBTN_N signal on PC Carrier Board; 5VSTB at EC input
Unnamed: 9: PWRBTN_N pulses low on button press; 5VSTB = 5V
Unnamed: 11: If replacement does not resolve: suspect PC Module or AC-DC fault

Unnamed: 1: System Cannot Power On (Power Button Green Blink, No Rails)
Unnamed: 2: AC indicator ON. Power button pressed → green indicator blinks. 3.3V/5V/12V status indicators remain OFF.
Unnamed: 3: PC Carrier Board confirmed responding (green blink) — did PC Module receive and respond to power-on?
Unnamed: 4: PC Carrier Board sent signal; PC Module did NOT respond — PC Module failure (90% probability per manual)
Unnamed: 5: Run Self-Test Z0201; check Windows Device Manager for 'Ultrasound MultiFunction Device'. Replace PC Module Assembly (115-037338-00).
Unnamed: 6: No green blink observed — see PWR-002
Unnamed: 8: PC12V rail at DC-DC output (⚠️ AI INFERRED — specific test point not documented in manual)
Unnamed: 11: If PC Module replacement fails: may indicate DC-DC board issue — escalate

Unnamed: 1: System Cannot Power On (Power Button Yellow Blink)
Unnamed: 2: AC indicator ON. Power button pressed → yellow indicator begins blinking.
Unnamed: 3: Are any power rails (3.3V/5V/12V indicators) present after yellow blink?
Unnamed: 4: No rails present — DC-DC Board failure (90% probability per manual). DC-DC fails to respond to EC enable signal.
Unnamed: 5: Run Self-Test Z0301 (Front-End Voltage Monitor). Replace DC-DC Board (115-025761-00).
Unnamed: 6: Some rails present — partial DC-DC failure or rail-specific fault (⚠️ AI INFERRED)
Unnamed: 7: Run Z0301 to identify which specific rail is out of spec; isolate and replace DC-DC Board
Unnamed: 8: DC-DC output rails via ADT7462 / Self-Test Z0301: D5V, D3V3, A5V7, A6V, A2V1, 12V_ACDC
Unnamed: 9: All rails within spec per Z0301 test limits (specific limits ❌ NOT DOCUMENTED explicitly in manual text)
Unnamed: 11: If DC-DC replacement does not resolve: escalate to Mindray

Unnamed: 1: No Echo in Ultrasound Image (Probe Recognized, No Echo)
Unnamed: 2: System starts normally. Probe is recognized. B-mode scan produces completely black image — no echo return.
Unnamed: 3: Is PHV voltage output from PHV module 0V or abnormal? (Check LOG at D:\DC70\LOG for PHV alarm entries)
Unnamed: 4: PHV output 0V or out of range — PHV Board or DC-DC Board failure
Unnamed: 5: Run Self-Test Z0603 (PHV Mode) and Z0604 (HV Test ±100V). Replace Power Box (115-047000-00) or DC-DC Board (115-025761-00).
Unnamed: 6: PHV appears normal — TR64 Board failure (higher probability) or Probe Board failure (lower probability)
Unnamed: 7: Run Self-Test Z0404 (TRA TX/RX Function Test) and Z0403 (TRA AFE Test Mode). Replace TR64 Board (115-033345-00) first; if no change, replace Probe Board (115-033365-01).
Unnamed: 8: PHV1P, PHV1N, PHV2P, PHV2N via PHV serial port (Z0603); ±100V HV via Z0604
Unnamed: 9: +100V rail: 95–105V ✅ Verified | -100V rail: 95–105V ✅ Verified | PHV mode voltages: per preset limits (❌ specific values not documented)
Unnamed: 10: TR64 Board → DC-DC Board → Probe Board (in order of probability)
Unnamed: 11: If all three replacements fail: Engine Board FPGA or firmware issue — escalate to Mindray factory support

Unnamed: 1: Dark Strips / Line Dropout on B Image
Unnamed: 2: Vertical dark lines or bands visible on B-mode image.
Unnamed: 3: Are the dark strips fixed in position when switching between different probes on the same socket?
Unnamed: 4: Strips fixed regardless of probe — TR64 Board channel failure
Unnamed: 5: Run Self-Test Z0404 (TRA TX/RX). Confirm strip is channel-mapped. Replace TR64 Board (115-033345-00).
Unnamed: 6: Strips move with probe, or inconsistent — Probe malfunction (array element damage)
Unnamed: 7: Switch probe to different socket. If strip follows probe → probe fault. Replace probe.
Unnamed: 8: Self-Test Z0404 output: open-circuit or short-circuit channel messages
Unnamed: 9: No 'Open circuit of transmitting and receiving channel: XXX' or 'Short circuit' messages
Unnamed: 10: Replace Probe → Replace TR64 Board → Replace Probe Board Assembly (if strip inconsistent for single probe across sockets)
Unnamed: 11: No escalation unless all replacements fail

Unnamed: 1: PHV Hardware Protection Triggered (OVP / OCP / HV_PRN_N)
Unnamed: 2: Alarm popup: 'Alarm! high-voltage transmission is abnormal, and images display normally!' LOG: PHV hardware protection entry.
Unnamed: 3: Does system restore normal operation after restart and retest?
Unnamed: 4: System restores on restart — transient PHV protection event
Unnamed: 5: Monitor LOG for recurrence. If recurring, proceed as NO path.
Unnamed: 6: Protection triggers again after restart — PHV Board failure
Unnamed: 7: 1) 🔴 IMMEDIATELY cut power after shutdown. 2) Run Z0601/Z0602/Z0603/Z0604. 3) Replace PHV Board (within Power Box 115-047000-00). 4) Restart and verify.
Unnamed: 8: PHV1P, PHV1N, PHV2P, PHV2N via PHV serial port; CW-1P, CW-1N; ±100V rails
Unnamed: 10: Power down → Replace PHV Board (within Power Box 115-047000-00) → Restart and verify
Unnamed: 11: PHV protection recurs after board replacement — possible TR Board or probe short circuit. Escalate to Mindray immediately.

Unnamed: 2: System starts BIOS, then 'OPERATING SYSTEM NOT FOUND' appears. OS does not load.
Unnamed: 3: Is the HDD physically detected in BIOS boot device list?
Unnamed: 4: HDD detected but OS partition corrupted
Unnamed: 5: Attempt OS restore procedure (Chapter 6.2). Replace CRC_Result.txt if Z0101 still fails after restore.
Unnamed: 7: Check SATA cable connection at Port 0; check HDD bracket seating (Section 9.3.11). Re-seat. If no resolution: replace HDD (variant-specific FRU).
Unnamed: 8: BIOS boot device list (⚠️ AI INFERRED — no SATA signal test documented)
Unnamed: 9: HDD visible in BIOS boot device list
Unnamed: 10: OS restore (Ch. 6.2) → HDD replacement (FRU: 115-033332-00 to 115-037260-00 by variant)
Unnamed: 11: If OS restore repeatedly fails: HDD sector failure — replace HDD and restore again

Unnamed: 2: ECG functions unavailable or disabled in software; ECG menu non-responsive.
Unnamed: 3: Does Self-Test Z1401 (ECG Board Interconnection Test) PASS?
Unnamed: 4: Z1401 PASS — communication OK; possible ECG_12V power issue
Unnamed: 5: Check ECG cable connection physically. Run Z1402 (ECG Board Self-Test). If Z1402 FAIL: replace ECG Assembly.
Unnamed: 6: Z1401 FAIL — communication error between ECG Board and Engine Board
Unnamed: 7: Confirm ECG module physically installed. Check cable seating. Replace ECG Assembly (Optional FRU §10.2.1).
Unnamed: 8: ECG serial port UART communication; ECG_12V power supply (❌ voltage value not documented)
Unnamed: 9: Z1401: PASS | Z1402: PASS (all sub-tests: A/D, Flash, DRAM, CPU, Watchdog, Voltage_33)
Unnamed: 10: Check/replace ECG cable → Replace ECG Assembly
Unnamed: 11: If Engine Board serial port confirmed failed (not ECG assembly): escalate — Engine Board replacement required

Unnamed: 2: System alarm: 'Please contact service engineers if fans need maintenance.' LOG: Fan alert with fan name and current RPM below limit.
Unnamed: 3: Is the fan physically blocked by dust or disconnected?
Unnamed: 5: Power down. Inspect fan visually. Clean dust mesh (Ch. 12.2.1). Reconnect cable. Reinstall fan.
Unnamed: 6: Fan unblocked but RPM still below limit — fan bearing/motor failure
Unnamed: 7: Run Self-Test Z0205 (Fan Speed Test) to identify failing fan by ID. Replace specific fan: Outlet=115-042898-00 (9.3.9), Inlet=115-042896-00 (9.3.16), CPU=024-000518-00 (9.3.19), AC-DC Fan=115-042950-00 (9.3.23).
Unnamed: 8: Fan RPM via ADT7462 / Self-Test Z0205. Fan IDs: FS_TOP_TACH0/1/2 (top), FS_DOWN_TACH0/1/2 (bottom), FS_PC
Unnamed: 9: Each fan RPM above its defined minimum limit (❌ specific RPM limits not stated in manual text)
Unnamed: 10: Clean dust mesh (Ch. 12.2.1) → Replace failing fan → Reconnect circuit
Unnamed: 11: If temperature alarms persist after fan replacement: thermal interface issue — escalate
